output.title: Spot duplicate emails before they create cleanup work
output.body:
If you run a small business, duplicate emails are not mainly a tech problem. They are a workflow question: do the repeats reach you before you act on them?

Start with the last three duplicate examples you remember. Note where each one came from: the same contact appearing twice, the same person sending again, or you copying the thread into another tool. Then mark which repeats must be caught before any action, and which can wait for later cleanup. An invoice or payment request belongs in the first group. A newsletter usually does not. Human approval stays in place for anything involving money or other high-risk decisions.

One practical next step is a one-week manual test. Put suspicious duplicates into one folder and review them by hand. Count how many are real repeats, how many are false positives, and how much time the review takes. That gives you a plain answer on whether the problem is worth any automation at all, or whether the first fix is just a clearer definition of “duplicate.” Small problem, small test, no drama.
